lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Comprehende

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This is a tool that helps us, humans understand (comprehend) AI code changes, such as PR diffs, or per-turn changes, or any diff that we define. Reading PR diffs line by line, in alphabetical order never made sense, and it's time we do something about it, provide us with a way of reviewing code changes in a scalable, easy to digest form, without losing on fidelity.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Background

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: AI agents write more code than humans can review line by line. This tool moves review from cognitive surrender to cognitive offloading. The [glossary](./docs/glossary.md) defines both. The full argument is in the README.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## What the tool is

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: It's a review assistant tool, which users can run as a skill (invoked using slash command). This will take a diff (PR, turn diff, or anything needing a review), analyze it, find review groups and visualize them on a web UI.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Goals

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - 100% accuracy: live git wins. The review document is interpretation only.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Easy on the eyes, easy to read

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: - Allow drilling down to full files instead of the diff, git blames, commit messages, branches, and the sources the skill read

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: - Useful summaries of the issues and other sources.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - UI is always the same, not generated on the fly. Only the data changes.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Works locally, no need for hosted services, deployed packages

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Simple easy-to-understand wording throughout the UI and in the generated answers, using ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Glossary

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Read [docs/glossary.md](./docs/glossary.md) before editing the skill, the schema, the review code, or UI copy.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: When this file speaks, it uses these words:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `you` means the agent that reads this file and changes the code.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `we` means Máté and the people who build Comprehende.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `user` means the person who runs Comprehende to review a change.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `agent` means the coding agent whose change is under review. In some cases that also means you.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The rest of this file gives good defaults, not hard rules. The developer's choice wins over any rule here. If a rule fights the task in front of you, say so loudly and get a human sign-off before you break it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## How it works

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The CLI indexes `base...head` and writes a covering skeleton `review.json`: one path per changed file, stub prose, hunk refs. The skill fills interpretation only: title, groups, summaries, lookFor, sources. `validate` checks refs and coverage. `serve` and `export` share one UI and one git payload. Live git wins.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Where code lives

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `skills-next/comprehende/` - skill source. The only skill text you edit.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `src/schema/` - review document schema. The source of truth. Parse at the boundary, infer inside.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `src/review/` - grouping logic: `review`, `pregroup`, `digest`, `show`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `src/cli/`, `src/server/`, `src/git/` - CLI, serve/export payloads, live git reads.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `src/ui/` - fixed UI. Only the data changes.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `eval/cases/`, `scripts/eval/` - eval cases and runner.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `scripts/` - `fixture`, `sync-skill`, schema build.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Project rules

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Whenever you create or edit `skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md`, or run `pnpm release:skill` or `pnpm sync:skill`, read and follow the `writing-for-agents` skill first.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: The skill reviews any git repository. Write its rules so they fit any diff. Keep this repo's layers, modules, and product out of those examples.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Component look lives on the component. Tailwind first. If a bit of CSS is required, colocate it with that component using a CSS module. A component must not import a global stylesheet. Do not add descendant selectors in `styles.css` to style markup a component already owns. `styles.css` holds globals such as variables and themes. Exception: `src/ui/lib/gap-style.ts` may use descendant selectors to style Pierre markup.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: If the UI already shows the state, do not add a sentence that narrates it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Type safety helps humans and agents alike. Parse at the boundary, where the schema is the source of truth, and infer everywhere inside. If a bug could have been a type error, make it one before fixing it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## The three ways to hurt yourself

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 1. **Editing generated copies.** `skills/comprehende/` and `.agents/skills/comprehende/` are outputs of `pnpm release:skill` and `pnpm sync:skill`. Never edit them by hand. Leave `fixtures/` output alone too.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 2. **Running the full eval by habit.** Full `pnpm eval` needs `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY`, costs money and time, and CI runs it when it matters. Default to `pnpm eval -- --tag smoke --no-graders`. Run the full suite only for a skill redesign, and only when asked.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 3. **Storing patch text.** The review document holds interpretation and hunk refs, never diff content. Live git wins. Never invent a hunk ref, never paste patch text into `review.json`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Before calling work done

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The most common defect here is a change that fixes one layer and misses the rest. Walk this list and say which entries applied:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Skill.** Does the rule still fit any repo, in simple words?

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Schema.** Does `src/schema/` still accept what the skill writes?

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Review code.** Do `review`, `pregroup`, `digest`, `show` still agree with both?

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **UI.** The UI is fixed, only data changes. Does the existing UI show the new data with no narration?

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Eval.** Do cases under `eval/cases/` still expect the current behavior?

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Docs.** Check whether the change makes existing guidance wrong. See Documentation below.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Verifying

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Smallest proof that the change works. Focused tests for the files you touched (`vp test run <files>`), and `vp check <files>` for format, lint, and types on the files you changed.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not run repo-wide checks unless asked. No full `vp test`, no full `vp check`, no full `pnpm eval`. CI owns the full suite.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Test observable behavior, not implementation. Do not render components to static markup to assert props, and do not add tests that only mirror the code.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Ask before you verify with a browser or computer use. Do not spin up extra dev servers from subagents.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Documentation

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Most code changes do not need a docs change. Agents can read the code.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `README.md` is for people who use the tool. Change it when a command, install step, or other user-visible behavior changes. Leave it alone for internal implementation.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `docs/` is for decisions and traps that code alone does not show: why a rule exists, what spans components, what is easy to get wrong. If reading the code answers the question, leave it out.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not list every field, narrate control flow, keep file catalogs, or append PR summaries. Link to source instead of copying it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - When a documented decision changes, rewrite or remove the old text. Do not append a second account of the new behavior.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Plans and work artifacts

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not commit implementation plans, research notes, or agent scratch files. Keep temporary work outside the worktree.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - A merged PR is the implementation record. Do not keep a second checklist in the repo.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Releases happen manually. Do not change `package.json` version unless the user asks for a release. When they do, follow the Release section in [README.md](./README.md). The release commit subject is the version. The body is the release notes: every user-visible CLI, UI, and skill change since the previous version, taken from `git log <previous>..HEAD`.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: ## Pull requests

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Never make a PR unless the developer explicitly asks you to.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - When opening a pull request, run the local built CLI `comprehende review --data <path>` to write the covering skeleton (one path per changed file, stub prose). Fill interpretation with the comprehende skill from skills-next. Do not paste hunk refs by hand. Export the review, then host that folder with the pages skill. Put the printed URL in the PR body.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: After a change under `skills-next/comprehende/`, `src/schema/`, or `src/review/`, run `pnpm eval -- --tag smoke --no-graders` and paste the summary lines in the PR body. Needs `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY`. Exit 1 means validate broke or an expect drifted from current product. Smoke does not run graders.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: A merge to `main` that touches those paths (or `scripts/eval/`, `eval/cases/`) runs the full graded suite: workflow `.github/workflows/eval.yml`, repo secret `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY`. A failed job is the regression ping. If that secret is unset, the workflow skips; launch a cloud agent after the merge and run `pnpm eval`. Manual full suite is for skill redesign.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Eval commands, run times, and what to do when a run aborts: [docs/eval.md](./docs/eval.md). Read it before you run `pnpm eval`.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Judgement rules for review: [.cursor/BUGBOT.md](./.cursor/BUGBOT.md).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Notes from Máté, the repo owner

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: I love to see simple code solving real, complex problems. Make every change, design, and text in that spirit. The skill is reviewed and adjusted by me manually, but write it with these principles in mind too.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: I don't want this project to get overly complicated. In practice this means I want to keep the code focusing on the universal Git part, not specifics of any Git forge or issue tracker - those must be handled at the skill level.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: Watch out for small, quick neat wins and the attention to detail that makes people say wow, that's cool.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: ## Cursor Cloud specific instructions

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: To open the mixed fixture UI (colored Overview stories and lookFor) without writing `review.json`: run `pnpm fixture`, then the printed serve command from that cwd. The process prints the URL (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`).

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.text: UI smoke for that fixture (`#overview` and one `#group/...`, then exit): `pnpm fixture:smoke`.
